title: Humanoid.Died
summary: Fires once when a character's health hits zero. Death handling belongs here — but remember each respawn brings a NEW Humanoid, so reconnect it on every CharacterAdded.

details.heading: One-shot per Humanoid
details.body: Each Humanoid instance fires Died exactly once. Respawns create new Humanoids — re-subscribe via CharacterAdded.

explanation.whatItIs: The moment-of-death hook: kill feeds, score credits, respawn timers, drop loot.
explanation.whyItExists: Death is THE pivot event in most games; one clean signal marks it.
whenToUse: Killer attribution (track last-damager yourself — Died passes no arguments)
Round logic (all players dead → round over)
Cleanup: ragdolls, death cameras, respawn delays
whenNotToUse: As damage detection — use HealthChanged/TakeDamage wrappers
Expecting it to tell you WHO killed — it doesn't; record damage attribution yourself
tips: Server-side only for authority (clients can fake local deaths)
Track last-hit source in a table keyed by character for kill credits
Died → task.wait(respawnDelay) → LoadCharacter for custom respawn timing (or use Players.RespawnTime)
commonMistakes: Connecting once per player instead of per character
Expecting arguments (who/what killed) — Died provides none
Acting on client-side Died for rewards — exploiters die on demand

examples.title: Death counting with proper lifecycle
